| n1-baseline-matrix-384 | leaderboard | 18 | exploratory | Results | At the preregistered 20 m buffer the best single pass for mound localisation is genuine Gemini 3 Pro text at T=0.0. Tier 1 -- the tie_set -- is a two-member statistical tie between pro-text-high-t-0-0 (F1 0.804) and pro-text-medium-t-0-0 (F1 0.792): a round-robin tile-swap permutation (BH-FDR q=0.05; 129/153 pairs significant -> 7 tiers) cannot separate them, and both are significantly clear of the Tier-2 pair -- the two Pro-text T=0.7 cells, pro-text-medium-t-0-7 (0.755) and pro-text-high-t-0-7 (0.745). So at T=0.0 the thinking level (HIGH vs MEDIUM) does not significantly matter, and T=0.0 beats T=0.7 (Tier 1 vs Tier 2) at matched model and modality (H7). The top four cells are all Pro text and the top six all genuine Pro; the text-over-image advantage holds at matched settings (best Pro text 0.804 vs best Pro image 0.666). The F1 leaders are NOT the tile-level discrimination (MCC) leader: genuine Pro IMAGE wins MCC -- pro-image-medium-t-0-7 (MCC +0.911, but 9th on F1) and pro-image-high-t-0-0 (+0.868) -- while Pro text leads F1, so the best single-pass configuration is metric-dependent. (All eight Pro cells are genuine Gemini 3 Pro at n>=3; see deviations E57 and docs/methodology/n1-baseline-matrix.md for board provenance.) |

| diversity-dividend-384 | leaderboard | 22 | exploratory | Results | Both named claims of the diversity-dividend test are confirmed at the preregistered 20m buffer. Per the preregistered H3 analysis plan (analysis-summary.md: 'compare voted F1 vs single-pass mean F1' + 'threshold sweep curves showing optimal (N, threshold) combinations'), the headline is each configuration's BEST (N, threshold) operating point against the known test-tile ground truth -- the study's purpose is to characterise how well VLM symbol extraction localises mounds, so best-achievable performance is the deliverable, not a confound. Method: round-robin tile-swap permutation (10k perms, seed 42, two-sided; BH-FDR q=0.05) + greedy-clique tiering over a 22-cell board (4 consensus champions + 18 single-pass cells); 197/231 pairs significant -> 7 tiers. (1) DIVERSITY DIVIDEND -- HIGH-thinking consensus significantly exceeds minimal-thinking consensus at matched modality: text +0.153 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.239) and image +0.070 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.272). The HIGH-thinking pools take the larger consensus gain -- more varied proposals let a high vote threshold prune their false positives. (2) CONSENSUS vs SINGLE-PASS -- every consensus champion significantly beats its matched within-pool single-pass baseline (+0.13 to +0.43 F1, all BH-p<0.001), and the lift persists at the production N=5 operating point (text 4-of-5, image 3-of-5; +0.09 to +0.33 F1). (3) CROSS-ARCHITECTURE HEADLINE -- Tier 1 (the tie_set) is a THREE-member statistical tie: the best Flash HIGH-text consensus (F1 0.814) and the two genuine-Gemini-3-Pro single-pass text leaders (pro-text-high-t-0-0 0.804, pro-text-medium-t-0-0 0.792); the permutation cannot separate Flash-consensus from the Pro leader (p=0.616, BH-p=0.66). Cheap Flash consensus reaches the expensive Pro single-pass tier on localisation F1. OPERATING-POINT SENSITIVITY (characterised, co-headlined): the Tier-1 parity is at the best (N, threshold) point (26-of-30); at the production N=5 carry-forward point (text 4-of-5) the same pool reaches TIER 2 (0.720), tying genuine Pro text at T=0.7 -- a best-minus-N5 delta of ~0.094 F1 (the within-test cousin of the carry-forward-vs-best delta the 55-map generalisation reports). F1-parity is NOT MCC-parity: the Pro text leaders are more tile-precise (MCC 0.790, 11 tile FPs) than the Flash consensus champion (MCC 0.620, 41 tile FPs) -- the metric-dependent-winner pattern of the n1 board persists. Deployment generalisation to unseen maps is the separate question answered by the 55-map runs. Era-2 487-tile test scope, 384px, gemini-3-flash. Artefacts: results/diversity-dividend-384/{tiering-champions,tiering-with-deployable}/tiering_20m.{json,md}; script scripts/consensus_vs_baseline_tiering.py; cell spec planning/diversity-dividend-cells-2026-06-06.json. |

| phase3a-high-consensus-calibration | sweep | 9 | exploratory | Results | Consensus calibration over 9 HIGH-thinking text configs (3 temperatures x N in {5,10,30}), 14-buffer + MCC, Era-1 340-tile. Best operating points cluster tightly near F1 0.77 at N=30: T1.0 23-of-30 F1=0.7747 (MCC 0.6425, the MCC leader), T0.3 23-of-30 F1=0.7744 (MCC 0.5759), T0.7 22-of-30 F1=0.7729 (MCC 0.5722). This is ~+0.08 F1 above the matched MINIMAL-thinking phase3a text consensus (~0.69) and substantially higher MCC (0.57-0.64 vs 0.15-0.33) — the diversity dividend: HIGH-thinking pools yield more varied proposals that a high vote threshold converts into both better localisation and far better tile discrimination. Best-F1@20m rises with N. Registers the calibration material; the formal HIGH-vs-MINIMAL test is retest-phase3a-replication and the 384px diversity-dividend-384 sibling. |
